key_insight: RL post-training does not need to update every transformer layer: training a single well-chosen layer can match the performance of full-parameter RL training. This suggests RL gains are highly concentrated rather than evenly spread across the network.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the assumption that reinforcement learning improvements in LLM post-training require updating all model parameters equally. It investigates where RL adaptation actually happens inside transformer layers and whether most layers are necessary.
method: Perform a layer-wise study of RL post-training by selectively updating different transformer layers instead of all parameters.
Compare single-layer training against full-parameter RL training to measure performance parity.
Analyze how RL adaptation is distributed across layers to identify where the most useful updates occur.
impact: For AI practitioners, this could dramatically reduce RL training cost, memory use, and implementation complexity. It also provides a new path toward more efficient and targeted post-training strategies for large language models.
visual_elements: Transformer stack diagram highlighting one trainable layer versus frozen layers
Side-by-side performance chart: single-layer RL vs full-parameter RL
Heatmap showing where adaptation is concentrated across layers
Simple workflow icon set for 'freeze most layers, train one layer'
paper_title: Is One Layer Enough? Training A Single Transformer Layer Can Match Full-Parameter RL Training
paper_authors: Zijian Zhang, Rizhen Hu, Athanasios Glentis, Dawei Li, Chung-Yiu Yau
